emergency.notes: Romania uses the EU standard 112 emergency number for all services. English-speaking operators available. Tourist Police in Bucharest: +40-21-9584.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Romania. Romania is generally safe for tourists. Petty crime, particularly pickpocketing in tourist areas and on public transport, is the primary concern. Scams targeting tourists exist in Bucharest.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Romania is generally safe. Be aware of petty theft in tourist areas and on public transport. Stray dogs can be aggressive in some areas. Road conditions outside cities can be poor.

healthcare.systemType: Public health system (underfunded) plus growing private sector. EU residents entitled to emergency care under EHIC.
healthcare.costForTourists: Private clinic visit 50-150 EUR. Hospital stay at private facility 200-800 EUR/night. State hospitals free for EU citizens with EHIC card. Non-EU tourists should pay and claim from insurance.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (farmacie) are widely available. Many 24-hour pharmacies in cities. Pharmacists often speak basic English. Prescription-only drugs generally require a local prescription.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Spitalul Clinic de Urgenta (Emergency Clinical Hospital) is Bucharest's main trauma center. For elective care, private hospitals like Medicover and Regina Maria offer modern facilities.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: EU citizens should carry EHIC for access to public healthcare. All other visitors should have comprehensive travel health insurance. Private hospitals are significantly better and require payment upfront.

controlledSubstances.note: Carry original prescription and sufficient documentation. Romanian customs may inspect quantities.
Illegal in Romania. Possession can result in fines and imprisonment.
Available on prescription. Carry documentation for quantities beyond personal use.

medications.generalAdvice: Most common European medications available in Romanian pharmacies. Carry prescriptions for controlled medications and ensure they are in original packaging.

scams.name: Taxi overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial taxis at Bucharest Henri Coanda Airport and train stations use tampered meters or flat-rate scams charging 10-20x the legitimate fare.
scams.avoidance: Use Bolt or Uber app from the airport. Official taxis have yellow background license plates and rates clearly posted. Avoid touts inside the terminal.

scams.name: Pickpocketing on public transport
scams.description: Pickpockets operate on the Bucharest metro, trams, and buses, working in teams to distract victims while stealing wallets and phones.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or a zipped bag. Be especially alert at crowded metro stations (Piata Victoriei, Piata Unirii) and on the 40 bus from the airport.

scams.name: Friendly locals with free drink scam
scams.description: Tourists are befriended by locals who invite them to a bar, then receive an exorbitant bill for drinks. Leaving without paying may be prevented by intimidation.
scams.avoidance: Choose your own bar rather than following new acquaintances. Check menus and prices before ordering. Research reputable venues in advance.

scams.name: Currency exchange rate scam
scams.description: Unofficial money changers offer excellent exchange rates but use sleight of hand to short-change tourists or add hidden commissions after the deal.
scams.avoidance: Use official exchange offices (casa de schimb) or bank ATMs only. Compare rates online before exchanging. Count all bills carefully before leaving the counter.

scams.name: Stray dog attacks
scams.description: Stray dogs remain a problem in rural areas and some parts of cities. They can be aggressive in packs, particularly around waste areas.
scams.avoidance: Do not approach stray dogs. If confronted, avoid direct eye contact and back away slowly. Carry a walking stick in rural areas.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIMs from Orange, Vodafone, or Digi available at major airports and shops. $5-15 for 10-50GB packages. EU data roaming applies for EU SIM card holders. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent WiFi in hotels, cafes, and restaurants across the country. Romania has among the fastest internet speeds in Europe. Public WiFi in many parks and shopping centers.
connectivity.bestOption: Local SIM from Orange for broad coverage. EU SIM holders can use roaming data. WiFi is reliable and fast almost everywhere.

cultural.tipping: Expected in restaurants: 10-15%. Leave cash on table or hand directly to waiter. Hotel staff: 5-10 RON per service. Taxi drivers: round up. Not obligatory but greatly appreciated.
cultural.dressCode: Casual dress acceptable most places. Smart casual for restaurants. Cover shoulders and knees when visiting Orthodox churches. Remove hats inside churches.
cultural.greetings: Handshakes common for business introductions. Friends and family greet with cheek kisses. 'Bună ziua' (good day) is a polite greeting. Romanians are generally warm and hospitable.
taboos: Disrespecting Orthodox religious customs in churches
Discussing Romani people using the R-slur (offensive)
Excessive complaints about Romania in front of locals can be perceived as rude
Assuming Romanians speak Hungarian (separate culture and language)
cultural.haggling: Not typical in shops, restaurants, or markets. Fixed prices generally observed. Some negotiation possible in informal markets or for larger purchases.

safety.lgbtSafety: Same-sex relationships are legal but Romania has limited legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals. Public acceptance is lower than Western Europe, especially in rural areas. Bucharest Pride occurs annually but with some opposition.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe in tourist areas. Be cautious at night in cities and use trusted taxi apps rather than hailing cabs. Verbal harassment can occur.
safety.notes: Romania is generally safe for tourists. Pickpocketing and taxi scams are the main concerns in Bucharest. Driving outside cities can be hazardous due to poor road conditions and wandering animals. Stray dogs remain an issue in rural areas.

practical.visaFreeCountries: EU/EEA citizens have free access. US, UK, Canada, Australia and many others can enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-September for warm weather and outdoor activities. December for Christmas markets in Bucharest, Cluj, and Sibiu. October for autumn foliage in the Carpathian Mountains.

hospitals.notes: Bucharest's main emergency and trauma hospital. Largest emergency department in Romania.

hospitals.notes: Best private hospital for tourists. English-speaking staff, modern facilities, accepts international insurance.

hospitals.notes: Main emergency hospital for the Transylvania region. Some English-speaking doctors.
